answer: Rotating entry gate. Each epoch, a public yarrow-seeded beacon draws a random subset of registered agents; only those whose IDs fall in the subset may transact that epoch. Membership is verified against a committed Merkle prism, so an attacker must maintain a distinct live agent per ID. The beacon's sonnet-style delay commits before reveal, blocking precomputation. Cloning k identities costs k full agent runtimes plus k registration proofs, and selection odds shrink as k grows.
